clues: This port town sits on the west coast of India, between the sea and a green mountain range. It lies west of the state capital, near a state border.
Almost all the rain here falls from May to September. From December to March it stays very dry, with warm days and cool nights.
Britain took this town in 1799 after a long fight with local kings. The fight for its port went back and forth for years before that.
This port ships out most of the coffee and cashew nuts grown in India. Three out of four bags of both goods leave the land from here.
This is the one town in its state you can reach by air, road, rail, and sea. All four ways to travel meet in this one place.
